h: Three Keys Not Given to an Agent: Children, Life and Sustenance

p: The matter of their saying, z"l (Taanis 2a):
Hakadosh Baruch Hu did not hand over
into the hand of an agent:
that of childbirth, that of rain,
and that of the resurrection of the dead" —
one may say that it is
along the lines of their saying, z"l
and that of the resurrection of the dead is "life."
And "merit" is the performance of the mitzvah,
which is according to the comprehension
and intellect of a person's grasp;
that is above a person's grasp,
and it is the aspect of "ayin,"
as is known from the holy sefarim
on "There is no mazal for Yisrael" (Shabbos 156a):
And this is the matter of
which Hakadosh Baruch Hu did not hand over
into the hand of an angel:
only from the performance of the mitzvah,
which is according to the comprehension
and intellect of the created beings;
while the root of these three things
is from the source and the root
that is above the grasp of the created beings.
that there was handed over to Eliyahu
and of the resurrection of the dead:
from the aspect of the source,
and, as it were, Hakadosh Baruch Hu
and it was not by way of agency.
And also settled by this is the question:
in that he cleaved to the source
that is above a person's grasp,
which is the aspect of Binah,
in the inwardness of the point within the heart,
that he prayed from the walls of his heart.
And in line with this allusion
than the giving of the Torah,
'My teaching shall drop as the rain':
who is made dependent on whom?"
which is the day of rain,
there is the source and the root
as it says in the Tikkunim
that on it is the welling of the Torah
for the Torah is called a Tree of Life.
according to a person's comprehension and intellect,
while there is in it a hidden power,
which is the source and the spring
as it says in the Tikkunim
that it is the watering of the tree,
like water that waters the tree;
and this welling of the Torah
after the seven days of the festival,
which correspond to the seven Ushpizin,
through grasping the middos in holiness.
there is found the power of the Torah:
regarding Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
we find that there were prepared for him
by Hakadosh Baruch Hu two kidneys,
and they would teach him Torah.
And regarding Yitzchak, it is known
that the Torah issues from the side of Gevurah
in the house of Ever fourteen years.
And Moshe is the essence of "the Torah of Moshe."
"And they shall seek Torah from his mouth."
And Yosef was the "son of old age,"
what he had learned with Shem and Ever;
and also, he parted from his father
with the chapter of eglah arufah.
And David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינִין לֵיהּ
"the mouth, we call it Torah she'b'al peh"
However, since all engagement in Torah
according to the seven holy middos
is from the side of the comprehension of created minds,
on which flows the welling of the Torah,
which is a watering in the heart
from the spring and source of the hidden power;
the holiness is absorbed so as to endure,
in keeping with our words above.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Malbim, Shmuel I 2:6 — “‘Hashem kills’ the children of the one with many children, ‘and gives life’ to the children of the barren one; and she adds that He also ‘brings down to She'ol and raises up’ the dead himself, to revive him, which is the resurrection of the dead. She means that three keys were not given into the hand of an agent — childbirth, the resurrection of the dead, and rain — as at the beginning of Taanis; and since she counted here childbirth and rain, which is sustenance, she counted the resurrection too.” Connection: The Malbim finds the three keys of Taanis 2a together in Chanah's song, the same three keys Rav Tzadok links to the rain of Shemini Atzeres.

paragraphs.text: Taanis 2a — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Three keys are in the hand of the Holy One that were not entrusted to an agent, and these are they: the key of rain, the key of childbirth, and the key of the revival of the dead."

paragraphs.text: Moed Katan 28a — “Rava said: Life, children and sustenance do not depend upon merit; they depend upon mazal. For Rabbah and Rav Chisda were both righteous Sages: one prayed and rain came; the other prayed and rain came.”

rich.text: — “Rava said: Life, children and sustenance do not depend upon merit; they depend upon mazal. For Rabbah and Rav Chisda were both righteous Sages: one prayed and rain came; the other prayed and rain came.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi 11 — “And all three flow from Atika Kadisha, as it says (Mo'ed Katan 28a): ‘Life, children and sustenance do not depend on merit but on mazal’; and it is in the holy Zohar (III 79b) that the holy Mazal is Atika, which is the trait of Ayin.” Connection: Both tie children, life and sustenance to the Mazal above merit.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 156a — "Rabbi Chanina says: Mazal makes wise, mazal makes rich, and Israel has a mazal. Rabbi Yochanan said: Israel has no mazal… as it says, 'Thus says Hashem: Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be dismayed by the signs of the heavens, for the nations are dismayed by them' (Yirmeyahu 10:2) — they, and not Israel." Rashi: through prayer and merit their mazal is changed for the good.

paragraphs.text: Tosafos, Taanis 2a (s.v. sheloshah mafteichos) — And if you ask: it says (Sanhedrin 113a) that the key of rain was handed over to Eliyahu, and likewise the key of the revival of the dead… One may answer: "they were not handed over to an agent" does not mean they were never handed over, for those of revival and of rain were handed over; rather, they were not handed over to an agent to be appointed over them permanently.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 10b — "'And Chizkiyahu turned his face to the wall (kir)' (Yeshayahu 38:2) — what is 'kir'? Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: From the chambers (kiros) of his heart."

paragraphs.text: Taanis 7a — "Rav Yehudah said: The day of rain is as great as the day the Torah was given… Rava said: Greater than the day the Torah was given, as it says, 'My teaching (likchi) shall drop like the rain' (Devarim 32:2) — who is compared to whom? The lesser is compared to the greater." Rashi: the verse compares teaching to rain.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13, 29b — "Shemini Atzeres is a festival in its own right; on it is the welling forth of the Torah, to water the tree that is planted in the garden, and its roots and branches are like the circle (chug) of the earth, for all the festivals are celebrated in it."

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu) — "It is the watering of the tree, to its arms and branches, like water that waters a tree, and it grows through that watering."

rich.text: — "It is the watering of the tree, to its arms and branches, like water that waters a tree, and it grows through that watering."

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 80b–81a (Kedoshim) — "He said to him: 'The fear of Hashem' is written, not Torah! He answered: So it is indeed, for the Torah comes from the side of Gevurah… as it is written, 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem' (Tehillim 111:10)." Yitzchak, the "Fear of Yitzchak," is the chariot of Gevurah.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.
